prompts.text: This week I want to get the device risk score flagging tampered or rooted phones at activation. Done by Friday is a first feature list covering root detection, emulator use and device fingerprint mismatches, plus a rough count of how many Q3 activations would have been flagged.

Main thing for me is the suspected mule-account network that came in on Friday: about 40 accounts receiving small transfers and cashing out within the hour. I want to map how far it spreads and hand a case pack to the investigators by Thursday.
I'm planning to analyse SIM-swap fraud patterns from the last six months, mainly the gap between a SIM swap and the first suspicious withdrawal. Is that sensible to scope for one week?

I need to validate the synthetic-identity model on the Q3 holdout. Identities stitched together from real and invented details are still getting through onboarding, so I want precision and recall by customer segment before Friday.

I'm writing the investigation SOP for account takeover this week. It needs to cover how an investigator confirms a takeover, freezes the account and what evidence to collect before contacting the customer.
Quantifying Q3 chargeback losses by fraud type so finance has a number before month-end.

Can we make time this week to review how fraudsters bypass our KYC checks? We've seen accounts opened with borrowed IDs and edited selfies. I want a list of the gaps so we can close them before the next onboarding release.

I'm building the transaction graph for the fraud ring the investigators flagged, with accounts as nodes, transfers as edges and shared devices or phone numbers as links. Goal for Friday is a view showing the ring's core members and how the money moves.

I'd like us to red-team our own fraud rules this week: think like an attacker and look for loopholes, like splitting payments just under a threshold or rotating devices to dodge velocity checks. Then write up which rules need tightening and who owns each fix.
Drafting a field-investigation plan for stolen devices: which regions to visit first, how field agents confirm a handset is the one reported stolen, and when to involve the police.
Building the device-fingerprinting feature pipeline so we can spot one handset being used to open lots of accounts.
My week is the weekly fraud overview dashboard plus a new tile showing account takeover attempts by channel. Is that one piece of work or two?
I want to work out how fraudsters are gaming the referral promo with fake accounts, and what it has cost us so far.

I'm thinking about adversarial testing for the device risk score. If a fraudster spoofs their device ID or factory-resets the phone, does the score still catch them? I'd like a short test plan written by Wednesday.

We need to interview two sales agents suspected of colluding with a fraud ring to register devices under fake identities. HR and legal have to be in the loop and the agents can't be tipped off beforehand. How should I plan the week around that?
I'm sizing our money-laundering exposure through mule accounts for the risk committee pack. Done means a loss estimate with a range and a one-page note on the method.
I need to set up a sandbox where we replay known phishing and social-engineering attack sequences against our alert rules to see which ones fire.
Planning to look at first-party fraud this week: customers who take a device, stop paying and then claim it was stolen. I want to find signals that separate them from genuine theft victims.
I want someone to look at insider fraud risk, meaning staff whose access lets them override fraud flags or reset customer accounts. Who should own that, and what's a sensible first step?
Short one: I'm training a model to spot SIM farms, racks of phones cycling SIM cards to create fake accounts at scale. I want the labelled training set agreed by Friday.
